findings.description: Both dry-run routes call worktree_fingerprint before returning. Its git diff HEAD command can execute a configured clean filter when inspecting a modified tracked file. --no-ext-diff and --no-textconv do not disable clean filters. Consequently, repository-configured code can execute and write files during a dry run despite the identity-probe guards. The adapter mirrors contain the same implementation.
findings.evidence_gap: The filter regressions exercise blob_shas and code_state, but do not cover worktree_fingerprint or a complete dry run against a dirty tracked filtered file.
findings.recommendation: Use fingerprinting that cannot invoke repository filters for dry-run paths, and cover the complete routes with a tracked-file filter marker regression.
findings.title: Dry-run fingerprinting can still execute repository clean filters
findings.validation: Static inspection only; no tests or reproduction commands were executed and no files were modified.
